purpose: Refresh primary-source evidence relevant to the already-claimed Nemotron 3.5 ASR target-runtime benchmark after the clay-direct-dev bridge blocker was resolved.

refreshed_findings: German de-DE remains explicitly supported by the multilingual release.
Official material still describes cache-aware FastConformer-RNNT streaming that processes new chunks while reusing cached encoder context.
Configurable streaming operating points remain 80/160/320/560/1120 ms.
A local NeMo-Speech.cpp GGUF route remains documented, so the benchmark does not require a remote inference API.
The current streaming state accumulates PCM and each ready chunk re-feeds all audio seen so far to the model.
The exposed rollback mechanism is decoded-token-prefix rollback, not evidence of persistent internal acoustic-state rollback.
A Qwen maintainer states that the current open streaming implementation did not use KV-cache reuse and is still far from an industrial implementation.

interpretation.hypothesis: For a long-running local Frankenstein voice organ, Nemotron's native cache-aware streaming may have a structural latency/resource advantage over the current open Qwen3-ASR streaming implementation as stream duration grows.
interpretation.counterhypothesis: Nemotron may lose on actual German-room recognition quality, footprint, CPU/GPU fit, or integration complexity; upstream architecture claims and H100/FLEURS results do not establish the target result.
interpretation.discriminator: Run the already-claimed Nemotron Q8 target benchmark on clay-direct-dev after the current matched Qwen3-ASR/faster-whisper comparator, using identical pinned German/non-speech audio and recording WER/CER, partial stability, first/final latency, RTF, memory, and false activation.
